title: Slow-cooker lemon chicken
subtitle: Bright and tender chicken thighs in a lemon and herb sauce
excerpt: Boneless chicken thighs cooked with lemon juice, zest, garlic, and thyme. The sauce is light and fragrant. Good with rice, couscous, or roasted vegetables.
sourceNotes: Lemon chicken is a widely made dish across Mediterranean cuisines, adapted here as a slow-cooker method. The combination of lemon, garlic, and thyme reflects Greek and Italian home-cooking traditions.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The chicken improves with resting. Make a day ahead, refrigerate, and reheat gently on the hob.

content.text: This is a light dish. The lemon keeps the chicken bright and the sauce thin rather than heavy. Use good-quality chicken thighs here and do not skip the zest; it carries more flavour than the juice alone.
Honey rounds the sharpness of the lemon without making the sauce sweet. One tablespoon is enough; more and the balance tips too far. The garlic mellows over the long cook and becomes almost mild.
Serve over rice, couscous, or with flatbreads. Roasted cherry tomatoes or steamed green beans are good alongside.

Place {{chicken-thighs-boneless}} of chicken thighs in the slow cooker. Add {{garlic}} of crushed garlic. Pour over {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock and {{olive-oil}} of olive oil. Add the juice and zest of {{lemon}} lemons. Stir in {{honey}} of honey. Tuck in {{thyme}} of thyme sprigs. Season with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper-ground}} of black pepper.

Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 4 to 5 hours. The chicken should be very tender. Discard the thyme sprigs. Taste the sauce and adjust the seasoning. If the sauce is very thin, transfer it to a small saucepan and reduce over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes.

rows.cause: Two lemons in a sealed slow cooker can make a noticeably tart sauce, especially if the lemons were large.
rows.fix: Stir in an extra teaspoon of honey to soften the acidity. Next time use just one large lemon or one lemon plus a tablespoon of orange juice.

rows.cause: The chicken and the stock both released liquid during the long cook.
rows.fix: Pour the sauce into a small pan and reduce it by half over high heat. It will become much more flavourful and concentrated.

rows.symptom: The chicken is falling apart too much
rows.cause: Boneless thighs can shred after 5 or more hours on LOW.
rows.fix: This is not a flaw; the shredded chicken absorbs the sauce well. Check at 4 hours next time and remove when just tender.

rows.cause: Four cloves in a sealed pot is a significant amount of garlic.
rows.fix: Use two cloves next time, or reduce the amount by half. The flavour mellows considerably the next day.

content.text: Lemon chicken appears in Greek, Italian, and French cooking in dozens of forms. The slow-cooker version is closest to the Greek avgolemono tradition of using lemon to lift braised poultry. It is a useful recipe to have because it feels more effort than it is and suits many different accompaniments.
